about: Deliberate behaviour changes made after the Python 0.2.2 record in python-cases.json was frozen. tests/parity.rs replaces the listed answers by corpus index before comparing, so python-cases.json stays exactly as Python left it. Each change gives its reason and every case it alters.

changes.change: Employment Hero Beam 'Reconciled' is not sent to the fund (26 October 2026). Beam reports Reconciled once it has cleared the employer's money, before 'Sent to fund' (yourpayroll Super Contributions Report; Reckon's Beam status guide), so a Reconciled row gets no remitted date. The profile then gained every other status the vendor lists (30 October 2026): 'Sent to fund with response' and manual 'Paid' are transmission evidence or the employer's assertion, so sent; 'Sent to fund with refund', 'Cancelled', 'Failed', 'Refunded', 'Not actioned' and 'Payment failed' do not establish remittance, so they get no date.

payroll_profile.name: Employment Hero / KeyPay - Detailed Activity Report
payroll_profile.notes: From 1 July 2026 Employment Hero may include Qualifying Earnings or OTE/QE columns. Those are calculation bases, not the operator-determined SG liability, so this profile selects only an explicit employer-super contribution column.

super_profile.name: Employment Hero / KeyPay - Super Contributions (payments)
super_profile.notes: The payments CSV carries a Status column at the far right. Beam statuses run Created, Submission accepted, Awaiting payment, Awaiting clearance, Reconciled, Sent to fund, with Sent to fund with response, Sent to fund with refund, Cancelled, Failed and Refunded as the other automated outcomes. A contribution outside any batch is Not actioned, and a manual batch runs Created, then Paid or Payment failed. None of them is a fund receipt date. Sent to fund and Sent to fund with response (a fund replied with warnings or notes) are transmission evidence only, and Paid is the employer's own assertion, so those dates are remittance dates and nothing more. Every other status does not establish remittance, so its row gets no remitted date; that is not proof that no money moved. Awaiting clearance and Reconciled (Beam has cleared the employer's money but not sent it on) remain pending even if an employer payment date is present. Sent to fund with refund says a fund rejected and refunded some contributions without saying which, so each contribution needs reconciling against the batch history before its row is given a date by hand. A status outside this list is refused rather than guessed.

row 3: matched super rows carry no payment date
super row 4: status 'Reconciled' does not establish remittance to the fund, so its payment date is not evidence of remittance and was not used

No payroll or clearing-house export carries a fund receipt date, so fund_received_date is written blank on every row. The checker's deadline tests receipt by the fund, not remittance -- fill that column in from your fund or clearing house before relying on any verdict it produces.
A dated part payment writes remitted_date and remitted_amount; sg_amount stays the amount owed. matched_amount separately records the total associated with the payday, even when the vendor supplied no payment date, and caps any fund receipt later added to the row. Where a match contains dated and undated super rows, remitted_date is conservatively the latest known date for the dated subtotal: the checker credits none of the subtotal before that date and only remitted_amount afterwards. An entirely undated match leaves both remittance fields blank but keeps matched_amount. The warning lines below still name every partial: <received> of <owed> matched and every "... has no payment date on record" figure.
